# `set_view_plan`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start the ViewPlan scheduling worker, either with a new inline plan or by re-running the plan the device holds.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc7fe0, StartViewPlan @0x40ba10 (64-bit build) |

With params containing plan_name, the device replaces its held plan with the supplied one and starts the worker. Without plan_name (omitted params, or params without it) the device re-runs its held plan, optionally updating the two plan flags. A success reply means the worker thread was launched, not that the plan ran or completed.

Side effects: Replaces or resets the held plan and plan flags, clears capture progress, disables the stack simulator if enabled, stops the demonstration function, starts the ViewPlan worker and, on the 64-bit build where model and process allow, sets the plan indicator LED from the launch result.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_view_plan"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Two forms. (1) Full plan: plan_name present, list required. (2) Restart: plan_name absent; re-runs the held plan and ignores any list supplied. Non-object params (null, scalar, array) are tolerated and behave as omitted; clients SHOULD omit params or send an object. [READ] |
| `params.plan_name` | string | no | - | Presence selects the full-plan form. Empty string is accepted. [READ] |
| `params.update_time_seestar` | string | no | "" | Date of last plan edit; the iOS app was seen sending YYYY.MM.DD (OBSERVED 2026-10-12; meaning and format are app-side only). Not validated and not used for scheduling. Missing or wrong type clears the stored value. [READ] |
| `params.plan_target_af` | boolean\|integer | no | held value (compiled initial false) | Autofocus per target. Integer 0 is false, nonzero true. Wrong type is rejected with 106. Absent keeps the held setting; committed only if the start succeeds past parsing. [READ] |
| `params.viewplan_gohome` | boolean\|integer | no | held value (compiled initial true) | Park at end of plan. The final go-home decision reads a device setting that may differ from this parsed flag, so this field alone does not guarantee the action. [READ] |
| `params.list` | array<object> | if `plan_name` present | - | Targets in start order (the worker does not sort). Every element MUST be an object. No count limit, uniqueness check or sort. Range: at least 1 item(s). [READ] |
| `params.list[].start_min` | integer | yes | - | Start, minutes after device-local midnight (unit INFERRED). Values of 1440 or more are accepted and run past midnight. Signed 32-bit; no range check, extreme values wrap in the deadline arithmetic. Range: >= -2147483648, <= 2147483647. [READ] |
| `params.list[].duration_min` | integer | yes | - | Duration in minutes (proved by the multiplication by 60 in the worker). Not range-checked. Range: >= -2147483648, <= 2147483647. [READ] |
| `params.list[].target_id` | integer | yes | - | Opaque id, stored as signed 32-bit although the app type is wider. No uniqueness check. Range: >= -2147483648, <= 2147483647. [READ] |
| `params.list[].camera_mode` | string | yes | - | Exact lowercase match. wide and dual require second_camera and mount; dual then forces capt_type 0 and wide_size_index 0. On the 32-bit build the member may be absent, a non-string is rejected with 105 and any string other than tele with 209 (parity not otherwise established). One of: `tele`, `wide`, `dual`. [READ] |
| `params.list[].skip` | boolean\|integer | no | false | A skipped target is not run but still takes part in overlap and day-selection arithmetic. Parse failure is ignored. [READ] |
| `params.list[].alias_name` | string | no | "" | [READ] |
| `params.list[].target_name` | string | no | "" | Bad type ignored. [READ] |
| `params.list[].target_ra_dec` | array<number> | no | [-999, -999] sentinel | RA in hours, Dec in degrees (INFERRED). Only the first two numbers are read. Absent, short or malformed values do not reject the plan; they leave the sentinel (a parsed RA may survive a failed Dec). No range or finiteness check. Real values have 32-bit float precision. Range: at least 2 item(s). [READ] |
| `params.list[].lp_filter` | boolean\|integer | no | false | Light-pollution filter. Bad type ignored. After the target's goto succeeds, true moves the filter wheel to slot 2 (LP) and false leaves it at slot 1 (IRCUT); not restored afterwards. A failed goto returns the wheel to its previous slot. [READ] |
| `params.list[].star_type` | integer | no | -1 | Bad type ignored. [READ] |
| `params.list[].mosaic` | object | no | - | Optional. Only inspected after both target coordinates parsed successfully; otherwise silently ignored, even if malformed. Not an object: ignored. No grid size or overlap member is consumed. [READ] |
| `params.list[].mosaic.star_map_angle` | number | no | -999 | Degrees. App 3.3.2 reads it from its native sky-map renderer for plan targets and for the sky-map mosaic goto (READ). In equatorial-mount display mode it is the sky-map rotation plus the last solve angle; otherwise it is the sky-map rotation minus the clockwise on-screen direction of celestial west from window right (READ, app 3.3.2 native library; see grid-and-movement.md R20a). It has no fixed cardinal meaning of its own. Wrong type is rejected with 102. Must be sent for the mosaic to be applied: when absent (sentinel -999) capture setup resets the mosaic parameters to scale 1, angle 0, which do not enable a mosaic (INFERRED). [READ] |
| `params.list[].mosaic.scale` | number | no | -999 | Dimensionless canvas multiplier on the camera frame size (READ; the term is INFERRED). When absent, the whole mosaic is treated as unset (and is not echoed in the event), even if the other members are given. No range check or clamp; the mosaic is enabled when abs(scale) > 1.01 or abs(angle) > 0.1. The app UI uses 1.0 to 2.0 (INFERRED). There is no fixed grid per scale. [READ] |
| `params.list[].mosaic.angle` | number | if `scale` present | -999 | Degrees (INFERRED); truncated to an integer for the grid planner. Read only when scale is present, where it is then required; otherwise ignored even if mistyped. No range check; the app UI uses -90 to 90 (INFERRED). [READ] |
| `params.list[].second_camera` | object | if camera_mode is wide or dual | - | Ignored for tele. Must contain a stack object. [READ] |
| `params.list[].second_camera.stack` | object | yes | - | [READ] |
| `params.list[].second_camera.stack.capt_type` | string | yes | - | Matched ASCII case-insensitively, unlike camera_mode. Maps to internal ids 0, 4, 5. Other names fail with 207. One of: `stack`, `startrails`, `timelapse`. [READ] |
| `params.list[].second_camera.stack.wide_size_index` | integer | yes | - | Unsigned comparison below 4; negatives are rejected. Range: >= 0, <= 3. [READ] |
| `params.list[].mount` | object | if camera_mode is wide or dual | - | Ignored for tele. [READ] |
| `params.list[].mount.tracking` | boolean\|integer | yes | - | [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 268 | The View function is working | `operation is in progress` |
| 536 | A ViewPlan worker is already running | `view plan is already running` |
| 106 | plan_target_af or viewplan_gohome present with a type other than boolean or integer | `expected bool param` |
| 102 | A recognized mosaic number has a non-numeric type, or mosaic.scale is present without a numeric mosaic.angle | `invalid params` |
| 207 | Any other full-plan parse failure (bad plan_name, list missing/empty/not an array, non-object element, missing or mistyped required target member, bad camera_mode, bad wide/dual nested member), or a retained-list restart with no targets. Default when no helper assigned a code. | `fail to operate` |
| 212 | Worker thread could not be created; the new plan and flags stay committed | `fail to create thread` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, restart-held-plan - Re-run the plan the device holds (OBSERVED, iOS app, 2026-10-12):

```json
{"id":7,"method":"set_view_plan"}
```

Request, inline-plan - Whole plan inline, one telescope-camera target (shape OBSERVED; values invented):

```json
{"id":8,"method":"set_view_plan","params":{"plan_name":"Example plan","update_time_seestar":"2026.01.31","plan_target_af":false,"viewplan_gohome":true,"list":[{"target_id":1790000000,"target_name":"Example target","alias_name":"Example","target_ra_dec":[12,30],"start_min":1200,"duration_min":90,"camera_mode":"tele","lp_filter":false,"skip":false}]}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_view_plan","result":0,"code":0,"id":8}
```

Reply, already-running:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_view_plan","error":"view plan is already running","code":536,"id":9}
```
